clue.text: Note return of the long story, including leading romantic weepie-maker

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for a long story is read from its end
the leading part of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of romantic is wanted
including means taking something inside, so the story's letters wrap around the romantic's opening letter

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a saga is a long story, here turned around
first letter of romantic

explanation.surface: A note about a long love story that is guaranteed to make its audience cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Weepie is British slang for a sentimental tearjerker film; here the weepie-maker is anything that makes your eyes water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas makes people's eyes stream, so it is jokingly something that makes you weep, like a tearjerker film.

clue.text: Caught in their machinations several times

definitions.note: loose: thrice is exactly three times

indicators.note: machinations are scheming manoeuvres, suggesting letters being worked into a new order

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has been trapped by other people's scheming over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: The C goes in with the letters of their before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrice is an old-fashioned word for three times, a small case of several repetitions.

clue.text: Enthusiastic study in technique

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, so the study sits within the technique

blocks.note: a den is a private study or retreat
an art is a skill or technique

explanation.surface: A keen pupil studying how a method works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent describes passionate, eager feeling, a near synonym of keen or enthusiastic.

clue.text: They make a pitch for the job

definitions.text: They make a pitch for the job

blocks.clueFragment: They make a pitch for the job
blocks.note: surface reading: job applicants pitching themselves to an employer
setter's reading: people who prepare a sports pitch for play

explanation.surface: Candidates selling themselves to win a position.
explanation.walkthrough: Making a pitch for a job sounds like applying for it; the real workers literally make the playing pitch ready for the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsmen tend cricket and football grounds, rolling and mowing the pitch so it is fit for play.

clue.text: Make a fuss about a part of the flight

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fuss word wraps itself around the little word a

blocks.note: to stir is to cause trouble or a fuss
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous passenger complaining about a portion of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A flight here is a flight of stairs, not a plane trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a run of steps, so one step is a single unit of it.

clue.text: Finish knitting garment for jumble sale

blocks.note: first meaning: to take the last stitches off the needle
second meaning: an unwanted item of clothing given away

explanation.surface: Completing a hand-knitted item only to send it off to the charity sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitters close off their final row by a technique of that name, and discarded clothing is called by the same phrase.

clue.text: Vessel is able to circle round a river

indicators.note: to circle round something is to go all the way about it, so one word encloses the rest

blocks.note: can means is able
taken as written
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: A boat capable of sailing around a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is a river in south-west England; the A that follows it in the answer belongs to CAN, which splits after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, and vessel is a general word for any boat or ship.

clue.text: Northerner initially operating in southern court

indicators.note: initially points at the start of a word, so just its opening letter is used
in places one piece within another, here inside the abbreviation for the court

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
CT is the standard abbreviation for court
first letter of operating

explanation.surface: A northern visitor who started out working in a court down south.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies at the northern end of Britain, so a Scot is a person from the north.

clue.text: Go past and grab more than you should

blocks.note: first meaning: to pass another vehicle on the road
second meaning: read as ..., to take too much

explanation.surface: Advice about a greedy driver who passes others and helps themselves to too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word into over plus take: taking over the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaking is passing another car, and the split form literally means taking in excess.

clue.text: Fellow American picks out finicky types

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
US stands for American, as in the US
to spot is to pick out or notice

explanation.surface: An American chap choosing which fussy people to single out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone overly particular about small details, a person who is finicky.

clue.text: Plug into port communication system

indicators.note: into means going inside something, so the plug sits within the port

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of promotion, an advertisement
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Connecting a cable to a computer socket to get a network working.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug and port pull towards computer hardware; plug is a promotional mention and port is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio transmits messages by electromagnetic waves, a long-standing system for sending messages.

clue.text: One who writes to the French leading trainer about horses

indicators.note: the leading letter is the one at the front, so only the opening of trainer counts
about can mean in a disordered state, so the following word is moved around

blocks.note: au is French for to the
first letter of trainer
horses rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter writer sending news to a top French racehorse trainer about the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoress is a woman writer, an old-fashioned feminine form of author.

clue.text: Puzzling questions about old sister's instruments

blocks.note: c is short for circa, about
O is the abbreviation for old
a nun is a religious sister
drums are percussion instruments

explanation.surface: Baffling queries about the drum kit that once belonged to someone's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Sister here is a nun, and the possessive just joins her to the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or a difficult problem, so these are baffling questions.

clue.text: Arranged spot check

indicators.note: arranged means put into an order, here a different order of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surprise inspection set up in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot check reads as one phrase; spot is the letters and check is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or restrain it, the same as bringing it to a halt.

clue.text: Wasting one's time at home

indicators.note: wasting suggests something squandered and broken down, so the letters fall apart and re-form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Idling away the hours around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: At home reads as the scene; home alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Store caught out in secret mark-up fiddle

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for caught leaves the fodder
to fiddle is to tamper with, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop is exposed for secretly inflating its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one C from secret mark-up and rearrange the remaining eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket is a large self-service shop, and store is a general word for a shop.

clue.text: Bit by bit? Bit by bite!

blocks.note: first meaning: gradually, a little at a time
second meaning: a piece taken as a mouthful

explanation.walkthrough: The second phrase splits the word into piece (bit) and meal (bite), a playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually in stages, while its parts literally pair a fragment with something eaten.

clue.text: Abandoned on shore with newsman

blocks.note: a strand is a beach or shoreline
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist left marooned on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stranded is left helpless and deserted, as if washed up with no way off.

clue.text: Hides the remedy with boss on the move outside

indicators.note: something on the move is shifting about, so the letters shift into new places
outside means wrapping around, so the shifted letters go round the remedy

blocks.note: boss rearranged
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A manager walks around while keeping the treatment secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it or make it hard to see.

clue.text: Sport's pills? Nine crushed and swallowed

indicators.note: crushing breaks something up, so the number's letters are broken and remade
swallowed means taken inside, so the pills enclose the mixed-up number

blocks.note: tablets are pills
nine rearranged

explanation.surface: Questioning an athlete's drugs: nine tablets ground up and taken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; the crushed nine sits between TABLET and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is a game played with bats and a light ball across a net.

clue.text: What's in it is secret, but one gets the picture

blocks.note: first meaning: the legal phrase for private proceedings
second meaning: a device for taking photographs

explanation.walkthrough: In camera is the legal phrase for a hearing held in private, so whatever is in it is kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's chambers held behind closed doors give the private sense, and the photographic device captures images.

clue.text: Tamper with the decoration, it's said

indicators.note: it's said points to the spoken form, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

blocks.note: a medal is a decoration awarded for service

explanation.surface: Interfering with the ornaments, so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in something that is not your business, much like tampering.

clue.text: Roguish maiden not wanted on demonstration

indicators.note: not wanted means left out, so that letter is dropped from what follows

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A cheeky young woman who has been banned from a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: Maiden looks like the roguish girl but only gives its cricket letter, which is struck off the front of the protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a playfully mischievous, knowing manner, close to roguish.

clue.text: For ten struggling in prison this is not all

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters of the number are jumbled
in puts the jumbled number inside the jail word

blocks.note: per means for, as in per day
a cage is a place of confinement
ten rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten inmates fighting in jail, and only some of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a share or portion of a whole, so by nature it is less than everything.

clue.text: Drink to father on getting trophy

blocks.note: a cup is a trophy
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to Dad after he wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after here, as in a down clue the father sits below the trophy. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a cup of tea, an informal everyday beverage.

clue.text: Natural encore from the choir

indicators.note: from signals letters drawn out of the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A choir singing an extra piece after its concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound bouncing back, a repeat produced by nature rather than by performers.

clue.text: Bad trip and ached horribly, but it cost very little

definitions.note: a clause; the answer is the adjective, as in 'it was dirt-cheap'

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the first word are spoilt into disorder
horribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters come out wrecked and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable budget holiday left someone aching all over, though it was a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Both bad and horribly signal the jumble, which takes trip and ached together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt-cheap means extremely inexpensive, so something dirt-cheap cost almost nothing.

clue.text: Leaning right back at last

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the abbreviation for right is read the other way

blocks.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, turned round
the end is what comes at last

explanation.surface: Someone finally tilting back to the right politically.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general tendency or inclination, which is what a leaning is as a noun.

clue.text: Ruin polished material? Not hard

indicators.note: material is the stuff something is made from, so these letters are raw material to rebuild
not means without, so the letter for hard is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Spoiling a glossy fabric that turns out not to be tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of polished and rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or ravage something, leaving it ruined.

clue.text: Mean to declare one's seniority

blocks.note: to aver is to declare firmly
age is how senior someone is

explanation.surface: Intending to announce how senior you are.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like a verb meaning intend, but it is the mathematical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An average is the arithmetic mean, the sum of values divided by their count.
